answer: Latency Ladder Registration. A new identity must answer timed micro-tasks at a meadow relay before it can post; response deadlines tighten each round, so parallel accounts split one operator's attention and miss windows. Each identity also seeds a lagoon archive it must revisit on a randomized schedule, and only identities surviving to the summit tier gain vote weight. An attacker pays sustained attention per identity, which scales linearly and cannot be pooled, making mass registration costlier than honest single-account use.
